message.content:
**On March 2, 2026 (with SEC filing dated March 1, 2026), The AES Corporation entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by a consortium led by Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP, part of BlackRock) and EQT Infrastructure VI fund, with co-underwriters CalPERS and Qatar Investment Authority.**[1][2][4][5][6]

This all-cash transaction values AES at **$15.00 per share**, equating to a total equity value of **$10.7 billion** and an enterprise value of approximately **$33.4 billion** (including proportional net debt of $22.7 billion as of December 31, 2025).[1][2][5][6] It represents a **40.3% premium** to the 30-day volume-weighted average share price prior to July 8, 2025, the last full trading day before initial media reports of a potential deal.[1][2]

Key transaction details include:
- **100% equity funding** by the consortium for the purchase price, with assumption of existing debt.[1][2]
- Expected closure in **late 2026 or early 2027**.[1][2]
- No anticipated impact on customer rates for regulated utilities such as **AES Indiana and AES Ohio**, which will remain locally operated, managed, and regulated by local, state, and federal authorities.[1][2]
- Addresses AES's capital needs for growth beyond 2027; without the deal, growth funding might require dividend cuts or new equity issuances.[2]

The deal follows reports of a potential acquisition dating back to mid-2025 and will take AES private.[5][6] No other mergers, acquisitions, consolidations, divestitures, takeovers, strategic reviews, or joint ventures involving AES appear in the search results for the April 2023 to April 2026 period.[1][2][3][4][5][6]
